'''Eric Bledsoe''' (born December 9, 1989) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Shanghai Sharks]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] (CBA). He plays the [[point guard]] position. After a season of [[college basketball]] with the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky Wildcats]], he was selected by the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] with the 18th overall pick in the [[2010 NBA draft]] and subsequently traded to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]]. Bledsoe had a four-year tenure with the [[Phoenix Suns]] between 2013 and 2017, before being traded to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].

==High school career==
Bledsoe attended [[A. H. Parker High School|Parker High School]] in [[Birmingham, Alabama]]. As a senior in 2008–09, he averaged 20.3 points, 9.4 rebounds and 11.5 assists per game, and helped lead Parker to a 5A state championship runner-up finish.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20111015085211/http://www.ukathletics.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/bledsoe_eric00.html Player Bio: Eric Bledsoe]</ref> Considered a five-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Bledsoe was listed as the No. 3 point guard and the No. 23 player in the nation in 2009.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20151003105236/https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Eric-Bledsoe-63746 Eric Bledsoe – Yahoo! Sports]</ref>

==College career==
[[File:Eric-Bledsoe.jpg|thumb|upright=0.7|Bledsoe warming up before a game in 2010 while he was at Kentucky.]]
Bledsoe played one season at [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] in 2009–10, and averaged 11.3 points, 3.1 rebounds and 2.9 assists in 37 games (35 starts) to help the Wildcats to a 35–3 record and Elite Eight appearance. He was named to the Sporting News SEC All-Freshman Team and was a CollegeInsider.com Freshman All-American. He scored in double digits 20 times, including four games with at least 20 points.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/eric_bledsoe/bio/ |title=Eric Bledsoe Stats, Video, Bio, Profile |work=NBA.com |access-date=October 1, 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151001110101/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/eric_bledsoe/bio/ |archive-date=October 1, 2015 }}</ref> In four NCAA tournament games, he averaged 15.3 points and set a Kentucky school record of eight made three-pointers in an NCAA tournament game against East Tennessee State in scoring a career-high 29 points (9–11 FG, 8–9 3 FG).<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.timesnews.net/Sports/2010/03/18/Bledsoe-s-eight-three-pointers-lead-Kentucky-past-ETSU-100-71|title = Bledsoe's eight three-pointers lead Kentucky past ETSU 100–71| date=March 17, 2010 }}</ref> Despite being a natural point guard, Bledsoe often filled the shooting guard role playing alongside fellow freshman [[John Wall]].

On April 7, 2010, Bledsoe declared for the [[NBA draft]], forgoing his final three seasons of collegiate eligibility.<ref>{{cite web|last=Tipton|first=Jerry|title=Five Cats declare for NBA Draft|url=http://www.kentucky.com/2010/04/08/1214797/five-cats-declare-for-nba-draft.html|work=Kentucky.com|access-date=April 16, 2013|date=April 8, 2010}}</ref>

===Grade controversy===
In September 2010, it was reported that Bledsoe may have been ineligible to play his one season for Kentucky when discrepancies were found in his high school transcripts.<ref>{{cite web|author1=Solomon, Jon |author2=Leech, Marie|url=http://www.al.com/sports/index.ssf/2010/09/records_differed_on_bledsoes_p.html |title=Records differed on Eric Bledsoe's Birmingham prep grades|work=The Birmingham News |date=September 14, 2010 |access-date=October 2, 2010}}</ref> The Alabama Public School System hired the independent law firm of White Arnold & Dowd to investigate claims that one of Bledsoe's grades was improperly changed.<ref name="closes book">{{cite news |last=Solomon|first=Jon|title=NCAA closes book on Bledsoe case|url=http://www.al.com/sports/index.ssf/2010/09/ncaa_closes_book_on_bledsoe_ca.html|work= The Birmingham News |date=September 28, 2010|access-date=April 16, 2013}}</ref><ref name="strange ruling">{{cite web|last=Brennan |first=Eamonn |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/CollegeBasketballNation/post/_/id/15704/the-strange-ruling-on-eric-bledsoes-grades |title=The strange ruling on Eric Bledsoe's grades|work=College Basketball Nation Blog |publisher=ESPN|date=September 24, 2010 |access-date=October 2, 2010}}</ref> His algebra grade had been changed from a C to an A, thus raising his GPA high enough that he was eligible for the NCAA.<ref name="strange ruling"/>

Though the investigators concluded that the instructor's reasons for changing the grade were "not credible", and that a significant number of his high school grades were written over to reflect higher grades, the school board voted to allow the grade to stand, and the NCAA declared its investigation of Bledsoe's eligibility closed the following week.<ref>{{cite news |title=Bledsoe Grade Change Questioned but Upheld (Published 2010) |work=The New York Times |date=September 25, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230727190856/https://www.nytimes.com/2010/09/25/sports/ncaabasketball/25bledsoe.html |archive-date=2023-07-27 |url-status=live |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2010/09/25/sports/ncaabasketball/25bledsoe.html |last1=Thamel |first1=Pete }}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Los Angeles Clippers (2010–2013)===
[[file:Eric Bledsoe.jpg|thumb|Bledsoe with the Clippers in 2011]]
During pre-draft workout, Bledsoe was touted for his quickness, ball handling ability, and ability to make three-point field goals. He was subsequently selected with the 18th overall pick in the [[2010 NBA draft]] by the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]], but was traded to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]]. In his first season, he averaged 6.7 points and 3.6 assists and started 25 games. As a result, he was named to the [[NBA All-Rookie Second Team]]. In his second season, due to the Clippers' acquisition of [[Chris Paul]], he played only an average of 11 minutes per game, with only one start, and his stats dropped. In fact, during that season, he ended up being assigned to the Clippers' [[NBA Development League]] affiliate team, the [[Bakersfield Jam]]. However, during his third season, his statistics ended up rising in spite of still being behind Chris Paul for most of the games that he played. Bledsoe also participated in the 2013 All-Star Game's [[Slam Dunk Contest]].

===Phoenix Suns (2013–2017)===

====2013–14 season====
On July 10, 2013, Bledsoe was traded to the [[Phoenix Suns]] alongside teammate [[Caron Butler]] in a three-way trade with the L.A. Clippers and the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] that sent the Suns' [[Jared Dudley]] and the Bucks' [[JJ Redick]] to the Clippers with two different second round picks going to the Bucks.<ref>{{cite web|title=Suns Complete Deal for Eric Bledsoe and Caron Butler|url=http://www.nba.com/suns/suns-complete-deal-eric-bledsoe-and-caron-butler|work=NBA.com|date=July 10, 2013|access-date=July 10, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131005003222/http://www.nba.com/suns/suns-complete-deal-eric-bledsoe-and-caron-butler|archive-date=October 5, 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref> On his opening night debut with the Suns, Bledsoe helped the team by getting 22 points, 6 rebounds, and 7 assists in a 104–91 victory over the [[Portland Trail Blazers]]. In his second game with the Suns, Bledsoe hit his first ever game-winning shot in an 87–84 home victory over the [[Utah Jazz]]. Before the November 19, 2013, game against the [[Sacramento Kings]], Bledsoe's shin collided with teammate [[P. J. Tucker]] during practice. He would miss six games before returning with 17 points, 6 rebounds, and 3 steals in a 112–101 victory against the Jazz on November 29, 2013. Bledsoe scored a then-career-high 28 points in a 116–107 victory against the [[Sacramento Kings]] on December 13, 2013. Bledsoe also got his first double-double with the Suns by scoring 16 points, grabbing 11 rebounds, and putting up 7 assists in a blowout 117–90 victory over the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] on December 23, 2013.

During the third quarter of the Suns' last game of 2013 against the Clippers, Bledsoe injured his left shin. What began as a shin injury eventually turned into a meniscus injury that would leave him sidelined for nearly two and a half months. His injury was a leading factor in the Suns signing former player [[Leandro Barbosa]] back onto the team for the rest of that season. Bledsoe returned to action on March 12, 2014, against the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20131122034806/http://www.nba.com/games/20140312/CLEPHX/gameinfo.html Notebook: Cavaliers 110, Suns 101]</ref> He started for the Suns again and racked up 17 points and 10 rebounds two days later in an 87–80 victory against the [[Boston Celtics]]. He continued to start for the team throughout the rest of the season. On November 14, 2019, Bledsoe scored 31 points, setting a new NBA career high, in a 124–115 victory over the [[Chicago Bulls]].

====2014–15 season====
On June 27, 2014, the Suns extended a qualifying offer to Bledsoe, thus making him a restricted free agent.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/suns/news/suns-extend-qualifying-offers-bledsoe-tucker|title=Suns Extend Qualifying Offers to Bledsoe, Tucker |work=NBA.com | date=June 27, 2014|access-date=June 27, 2014}}</ref> After months of deliberation and rumors concerning his future, Bledsoe and the Suns reached an agreement on a new five-year, $70 million contract on September 24, 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/suns-and-bledsoe-reach-multiyear-deal|title=Suns and Bledsoe Reach Multiyear Deal |work=NBA.com | date=September 24, 2014|access-date=September 25, 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/11583579/eric-bledsoe-phoenix-suns-agree-five-year-contract|title=Eric Bledsoe, Suns reach $70M deal |work=NBA.com | date=September 24, 2014|access-date=September 25, 2014}}</ref> In the Suns' 2014–15 season opener against the Los Angeles Lakers on October 29, 2014, Bledsoe recorded 16 points, nine assists, and six rebounds before he drew his second technical foul and was ejected with 30 seconds left in the third quarter. Despite Bledsoe's ejection, the Suns went on to win 119–99.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20141029/LALPHX/gameinfo.html|title=Suns rout Lakers 119–99 despite Kobe's 31 points|work=NBA.com|date=October 29, 2014|access-date=November 1, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141112171143/http://www.nba.com/games/20141029/LALPHX/gameinfo.html|archive-date=November 12, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On December 8, 2014, Bledsoe recorded his first career triple-double with 27 points, 11 rebounds and 16 assists in the 120–121 overtime loss to his former team, the Los Angeles Clippers.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20141208/PHXLAC/gameinfo.html|title=Clippers beat Suns 121–120 in OT on Griffin's 3|work=NBA.com|date=December 8, 2014|access-date=December 9, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141209122902/http://www.nba.com/games/20141208/PHXLAC/gameinfo.html|archive-date=December 9, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> On December 23, Bledsoe recorded his second career triple-double and first one without resulting in an overtime, as he recorded 16 points, 10 rebounds and 11 assists in the 124–115 win over the [[Dallas Mavericks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20141223/DALPHX/gameinfo.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 25, 2014|title=Bledsoe gets triple-double, Suns beat Mavericks 124–115|work=NBA.com|date=December 23, 2014|access-date=December 23, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141225052730/http://www.nba.com/games/20141223/DALPHX/gameinfo.html}}</ref> On January 21, 2015, Bledsoe recorded a career-high 33 points, along with 10 rebounds and 6 assists, in a 118–113 victory over the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150121/PORPHX/gameinfo.html|title=Bledsoe scores career high 33, Suns top Blazers 118–113 |work=NBA.com | date=January 21, 2015|access-date=February 21, 2015}}</ref> On February 26, 2015, Bledsoe recorded a near triple-double with 28 points on 11-of-16 shooting, 13 rebounds, and 9 assists, as well as 4 blocks and a steal in a 117–113 overtime win over the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]]. In doing so, he became just the ninth player in NBA history to record similar kinds of statistics during the regular season, as well as the first point guard to record 50% shooting for 28 or more points while recording 13 or more rebounds, 9 or more assists, 4 or more blocks, and at least one steal in a game.<ref>[https://www.numberfire.com/nba/news/4550/putting-eric-bledsoe-s-stat-line-from-last-night-in-historical-context Putting Eric Bledsoe's Stat Line From Last Night in Historical Context]</ref> On March 21, he scored a career-high 34 points in a 117–102 win over the [[Houston Rockets]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150321/PHXHOU/gameinfo.html |title=Bledsoe scores career-best 34 as Suns beat Rockets 117–102 |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=March 22, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150630065222/http://www.nba.com/games/20150321/PHXHOU/gameinfo.html |archive-date=June 30, 2015 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

====2015–16 season====
On October 31, 2015, Bledsoe was only two points shy from tying his career-high in points scored, finishing with 33 points and 6 assists in a 101–90 win over the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151031/PHXPOR/gameinfo.html|title=Bledsoe has 33 and Suns beat Blazers 101–90|website=[[NBA.com]] |date=October 31, 2015|access-date=November 16, 2015}}</ref> On November 12, Bledsoe was one assist shy of recording a triple-double, finishing with 26 points, 10 rebounds and 9 assists in a 118–104 win over the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151112/LACPHX/gameinfo.html|title=Knight, Bledsoe lead Suns past short-handed Clippers 118–104|work=NBA.com|date=November 12, 2015|access-date=November 13, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161103201740/http://www.nba.com/games/20151112/LACPHX/gameinfo.html|archive-date=November 3, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> On December 13, in a win over the Minnesota Timberwolves, Bledsoe recorded 23 points with nine assists plus four steals and tied a career-high with four blocked shots.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151213/MINPHX/gameinfo.html |title=Knight's 25 points lead Suns over Timberwolves 108–101 |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=December 18, 2015 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20160216094303/http://www.nba.com/games/20151213/MINPHX/gameinfo.html |archive-date=February 16, 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref> It was the NBA's first "four-by-four" (at least four rebounds, four assists, four steals and four blocks) by a guard since [[Dwyane Wade]] did it on February 28, 2009.<ref>[http://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/nba/suns/2015/12/13/suns-grind-out-victory-over-visiting-timberwolves/77003550/ Suns grind out victory over visiting Timberwolves]</ref> On December 29, he underwent successful surgery to repair a torn meniscus in his left knee and was subsequently ruled out for the remainder of the 2015–16 season.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/bledsoe-surgery-update Bledsoe Surgery Update]</ref> With Bledsoe out, the Suns managed just 11 more wins over the final three months of the season.

====2016–17 season====
[[File:Eric Bledsoe Suns.jpg|thumb|right|Bledsoe with the Phoenix Suns in 2017]]
On September 15, 2016, Bledsoe was cleared for his first five-on-five scrimmage play.<ref>{{cite web|last=Coro|first=Paul|url=http://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/nba/suns/2016/09/15/phoenix-suns-tucker-out-6-8-weeks-back-surgery/90427224/|title=Phoenix Suns' Tucker out 6–8 weeks for back surgery|work=azcentral.com|date=September 15, 2016|access-date=September 25, 2016}}</ref> He made his return to the court in the Suns' season opener on October 26 against the [[Sacramento Kings]]. In his first game since injuring his knee in December 2015, Bledsoe recorded 16 points, six rebounds, five assists and one steal in a 113–94 loss.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899412|title=Cousins, Gay lead Kings past young Suns 113–94|work=ESPN.com|date=October 26, 2016|access-date=October 30, 2016}}</ref> On November 2, he scored 20 points and hit the game-winning three-pointer in overtime to give the Suns their first win of the season with a 118–115 victory over the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899513|title=Bledsoe's 3 sinks Blazers in OT, 118–115|work=ESPN.com|date=November 2, 2016|access-date=November 3, 2016}}</ref> On November 27, he scored a career-high 35 points in a 120–114 loss to the [[Denver Nuggets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899696|title=Suns' rally falls short, Nuggets win 120–114|work=ESPN.com|date=November 27, 2016|access-date=November 27, 2016}}</ref> On December 13, he had a 31-point game in a 113–111 overtime win over the [[New York Knicks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899814|title=Bledsoe, Suns beat Knicks 113–111 in OT|work=ESPN.com|date=December 13, 2016|access-date=December 13, 2016}}</ref> It was his third straight 30-point game, thus becoming the first Suns player with three straight since [[Amar'e Stoudemire]] in March 2010.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://twitter.com/SunsBballComm/status/808895160675397632|title=@EBled2 has his third straight 30-point game...|work=Twitter|date=December 13, 2016|access-date=December 13, 2016}}</ref> On December 23, Bledsoe recorded 24 points and a season-high 11 assists in a 123–116 win over the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899895|title=Booker, Bledsoe lead Suns past 76ers, 123–116|work=ESPN.com|date=December 23, 2016|access-date=December 23, 2016}}</ref> On January 16, 2017, Bledsoe fell just short of his third career triple-double with 31 points, nine rebounds and nine assists in a 106–101 loss to the [[Utah Jazz]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900041|title=Johnson's big 4th quarter gives Jazz 106–101 win over Suns|work=ESPN.com|date=January 16, 2017|access-date=January 17, 2017}}</ref> Six days later, he recorded a career-high 40 points and a season-high 13 assists in a 115–103 win over the [[Toronto Raptors]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900084|title=Bledsoe's career day leads Suns over Raptors 115–103|work=ESPN.com|date=January 22, 2017|access-date=January 22, 2017}}</ref> He surpassed that mark on January 28 with a 41-point effort in a 123–112 loss to Denver.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900130|title=Bledsoe scores 41 but Nuggets beat Suns again, 123–112|work=ESPN.com|date=January 28, 2017|access-date=January 29, 2017}}</ref> Two games later on February 1, Bledsoe tied his career high with another 41-point effort in a 124–114 loss to his former team, the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899430|title=Griffin scores 29, Clippers bounce back to beat Suns 124–114|work=ESPN.com|date=February 1, 2017|access-date=February 2, 2017}}</ref> Bledsoe's three 40-points games within 11 days is the fewest days needed to post three 40-point games in Suns history—the record was previously 13, set by [[Charlie Scott (basketball)|Charlie Scott]] in 1973.<ref>{{cite web|last=Scheessele|first=Keith last night|work=brightsideofthesun.com|date=February 2, 2017|access-date=February 2, 2017}}</ref> In the Suns' last game before the [[2017 NBA All-Star Weekend]], on February 15, Bledsoe recorded his third career triple-double with 25 points, 10 rebounds, and 13 assists in a 137–101 win over the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900250|title=Bledsoe's triple-double leads Suns over Lakers, 137–101|work=ESPN.com|date=February 15, 2017|access-date=February 15, 2017}}</ref> On March 15, he was shut down for the remainder of the season after battling knee soreness.<ref>{{cite web|last=Somers|first=Kent|url=http://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/nba/suns/2017/03/16/suns-loss-home-sacramento-might-leave-mark/99242800/|title=Suns shut down Eric Bledsoe ahead of loss to Kings|work=azcentral.com|date=March 15, 2017|access-date=March 16, 2017}}</ref> He finished with career highs in points and assists.

====2017–18 season====
On October 22, 2017, just three games into the season, Bledsoe [[Twitter|tweeted]] out "I Dont wanna be here", which Suns general manager [[Ryan McDonough (NBA executive)|Ryan McDonough]] took as a slight against the organization and dismissed him from playing with the team. Bledsoe claimed that the tweet referred to being in a hair salon.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2740296-eric-bledsoe-told-suns-i-dont-wanna-be-here-tweet-was-about-hair-salon-per-gm|title=Eric Bledsoe Tweet Was About Hair Salon|work=BleacherReport.com|date=October 23, 2017|access-date=November 13, 2017}}</ref> On November 5, 2017, Bledsoe was fined $10,000 by the NBA for his tweet.<ref>{{cite web|last=Bordow|first=Scott|url=http://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/nba/suns/2017/11/05/nba-fined-bledsoe-10-000-tweet/833868001/|title=NBA fines Suns guard Eric Bledsoe $10K for tweet|work=azcentral.com|date=November 5, 2017|access-date=November 5, 2017}}</ref> That same day, it was reported that Bledsoe would return to Suns team facilities to work out with staff members.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/article/2017/11/05/eric-bledsoe-return-phoenix-suns-team-facilities-staff#/|title=Report: Eric Bledsoe to return to Phoenix Suns team facilities|work=NBA.com|date=November 5, 2017|access-date=November 8, 2017}}</ref>

===Milwaukee Bucks (2017–2020)===
On November 7, 2017, Bledsoe was traded to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] in exchange for [[Greg Monroe]] and a protected first and second-round draft pick.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/release/bucks-acquire-eric-bledsoe-phoenix|title=BUCKS ACQUIRE ERIC BLEDSOE FROM PHOENIX|work=NBA.com|date=November 7, 2017|access-date=November 7, 2017}}</ref> He made his debut for the Bucks three days later, recording 13 points and seven assists in a 94–87 win over the [[San Antonio Spurs]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400974924|title=Antetokounmpo leads Bucks past Spurs in Bledsoe's debut|work=ESPN.com|date=November 10, 2017|access-date=November 10, 2017}}</ref> On November 22, in his return to Phoenix, Bledsoe scored 30 points in a 113–107 overtime win over the Suns.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975015|title=Middleton scores 40 points, Bucks beat Suns in OT|work=ESPN.com|date=November 22, 2017|access-date=November 22, 2017}}</ref> On March 30, 2018, he scored 39 points in a 124–122 overtime win over the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975882|title=Bledsoe scores 39, Bucks beat Lakers 124–122 in OT|work=ESPN.com|date=March 30, 2018|access-date=March 30, 2018}}</ref> On April 9, 2018, he had his fourth career triple-double with 20 points, 12 rebounds and 11 assists in a 102–86 win over the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975954|title=Bucks close out Bradley Center with 102–86 win over Magic|work=ESPN.com|date=April 9, 2018|access-date=April 9, 2018}}</ref>

[[File:Bradley Beal, Eric Bledsoe (27935025389) (cropped).jpg|thumb|right|upright|Bledsoe in January 2018.]]

On January 19, 2019, Bledsoe scored 30 points in a 118–108 win over the Magic.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071358|title=Bledsoe scores 30 points, Bucks hold off Magic 118–108|work=ESPN.com|date=January 19, 2019|access-date=February 28, 2019}}</ref> On February 27, he recorded 26 points, 13 assists and 12 rebounds in a 141–140 overtime win over the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071593|title=Bledsoe has triple-double as Bucks edge Kings 141–140 in OT|work=ESPN.com|date=February 27, 2019|access-date=February 28, 2019}}</ref> On March 1, he scored 31 points in a 131–120 win over the Lakers.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071607|title=Bucks outlast Lakers 131–120 for 8th straight win|work=ESPN.com|date=March 1, 2019|access-date=March 2, 2019}}</ref> On March 4, he signed a four-year, $70 million contract extension with the Bucks.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/bucks-sign-eric-bledsoe-contract-extension|title=Bucks Sign Eric Bledsoe to Contract Extension|work=NBA.com|date=March 4, 2019|access-date=March 4, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Wojnarowski|first=Adrian|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/26114166/bucks-extend-bledsoe-4-years-70m|title=Sources: Bucks extend Bledsoe for 4 years, $70M|work=ESPN.com|date=March 1, 2019|access-date=March 2, 2019}}</ref> At the season's end, he was named to the [[NBA All-Defensive Team|NBA All-Defensive First Team]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/2018-19-all-defensive-teams-official-release|title=Gobert, George, Antetokounmpo lead 2018–19 All-Defensive First Team|work=NBA.com|date=May 22, 2019|access-date=June 24, 2019}}</ref> On December 14, 2019, the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] announced that Bledsoe had suffered from a right fibula avulsion fracture during a 127–114 seasons win over the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] and was expected to be sidelined for about two weeks.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/medical-update-eric-bledsoe|title=Medical Update On Eric Bledsoe|date=December 14, 2019|website=NBA.com|access-date=December 14, 2019}}</ref> Bledsoe helped the Bucks capture the best record in the league for the second consecutive season, however Milwaukee once again failed to appear in the [[NBA Finals]], losing to the eventual Eastern Conference champion [[2019-20 Miami Heat season|Miami Heat]] in five games in the Semi-Finals, with Bledsoe missing Game 1 due to a hamstring injury.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/29781631/bucks-eric-bledsoe-game-1-vs-heat-strained-hamstring|title = Bucks' Bledsoe ruled out with strained hamstring|date = August 31, 2020}}</ref>

===New Orleans Pelicans (2020–2021)===
On November 24, 2020, Bledsoe was traded, along with two future first round picks and two pick swap rights, to the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] for [[Jrue Holiday]] as part of a deal also involving the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] and [[Denver Nuggets]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Pelicans acquire Steven Adams, Eric Bledsoe in four-team trade|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-acquire-steven-adams-eric-bledsoe-four-team-trade|website=NBA.com|access-date=November 24, 2020|date=November 24, 2020}}</ref> In his debut with the Pelicans, Bledsoe recorded 18 points, two rebounds and six assists in a 113–99 win over the Toronto Raptors.<ref>{{cite web |title=Pelicans' Eric Bledsoe: Impresses in debut |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/pelicans-eric-bledsoe-impresses-in-debut/ |work=CBS Sports |access-date=January 29, 2021 |date=December 23, 2020}}</ref>

===Return to Los Angeles (2021–2022)===
On August 7, 2021, Bledsoe was traded along with [[Steven Adams]], the draft rights to [[Ziaire Williams]] and [[Jared Butler]], and a 2022 protected first round pick to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] in a three team deal with the [[Charlotte Hornets]]. The Pelicans received [[Jonas Valančiūnas]] and the draft rights to [[Trey Murphy III]] and [[Brandon Boston Jr.]] from Memphis.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-three-team-trade-with-pelicans-and-hornets-210807|title=Grizzlies acquire Steven Adams, Eric Bledsoe, draft rights to Ziaire Williams and two draft picks in three-team trade with Pelicans and Hornets|work=NBA.com|date=August 7, 2021}}</ref> On August 16, Bledsoe was then traded to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] for [[Patrick Beverley]], [[Rajon Rondo]], and [[Daniel Oturu]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/clippers/news/la-clippers-acquire-eric-bledsoe-memphis-grizzlies|title=LA Clippers Acquire Eric Bledsoe From Memphis Grizzlies|work=NBA.com|date=August 16, 2021}}</ref> On October 21, 2021, Bledsoe suited up as a Clipper for the first time since 2013, recording 22 points, along with 3 steals, in a 115–113 loss to the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401358778|title= Stephen Curry scores 45, Warriors hold off Clippers 115–113|work=ESPN.com|date=October 21, 2021}}</ref>

On February 4, 2022, Bledsoe was traded, alongside [[Keon Johnson (basketball, born 2002)|Keon Johnson]], [[Justise Winslow]] and a 2025 second-round pick, to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] in exchange for [[Norman Powell]] and [[Robert Covington]]. In Portland, he reunited with Trail Blazers coach [[Chauncey Billups]], whom he was teammates with during the [[2011–12 NBA season]] with the Clippers.<ref>{{Cite web |title=TRAIL BLAZERS ACQUIRE ERIC BLEDSOE, KEON JOHNSON AND JUSTISE WINSLOW |url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/trail-blazers-acquire-eric-bledsoe-keon-johnson-and-justise-winslow |access-date=March 27, 2022 |website=NBA}}</ref> On March 28, Bledsoe was ruled out for the remainder of the season with pain in his left [[Achilles tendon]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=TRAIL BLAZERS INJURY UPDATES |url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/trail-blazers-injury-updates |access-date=March 28, 2022 |website=NBA}}</ref> He was waived on July 6, having never played a game as a member of the team.<ref>{{cite web|title=Trail Blazers Waive Eric Bledsoe|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-waive-eric-bledsoe|website=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2022|access-date=July 6, 2022}}</ref>

=== Shanghai Sharks (2022–2025) ===
On November 19, 2022, Bledsoe signed with the [[Shanghai Sharks]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-11-19 |title=Alberto de Roa: Eric Bledsoe has signed with Chinese club Shanghai Sharks. pic.twitter.com/WOQ5QTf8g… |url=https://hoopshype.com/rumor/1804479/ |access-date=2022-11-20 |website=HoopsHype |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Bledsoe's mother, Maureen Reddick, worked several jobs and raised three children on her own in [[Birmingham, Alabama]].<ref>[http://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/nba/suns/2014/10/25/boivin-phoenix-suns-eric-bledsoe-focused-earning-respect/17886433/ Boivin: Phoenix Suns' Eric Bledsoe is focused on earning respect]</ref> Bledsoe has five children: sons Ethan and Emory and daughters Eriauna, Norah, and Noor.<ref>[https://twitter.com/Suns/status/712367024173744128 Family, Flexing and a Fighter...]</ref>

On October 27, 2022, Bledsoe was arrested in [[Lost Hills, California]] on misdemeanor charges of domestic violence.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Former NBA Player Eric Bledsoe Arrested on Domestic Violence Charges |url=https://www.yahoo.com/entertainment/former-nba-player-eric-bledsoe-193904446.html |access-date=2022-10-28 |website=www.yahoo.com |date=October 27, 2022 |language=en-US}}</ref>

On June 18, 2025, Bledsoe was arrested near [[Los Angeles]], [[California]] after allegedly striking a woman in the face.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Former NBA star Eric Bledsoe arrested after allegedly striking woman in the face|url=https://nypost.com/2025/06/18/sports/former-nba-star-eric-bledsoe-arrested-in-domestic-violence-case/|access-date=October 28, 2025|website=nypost.com|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Former NBA Star Eric Bledsoe Booked On Troubling Charges|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/article/former-nba-star-eric-bledsoe-234637170.html|access-date=October 28, 2025|website=sports.yahoo.com|language=en}}</ref>
